purpose: Review the three existing system-or-manager-only sources from the bounded 22-source inventory as exact-revision mechanism references without treating them as ordinary Skill candidates, executing them, or changing any live manager or consumer state.

cohortContract.coverageObjective: Test whether existing external manager, installer, orchestration, recovery, and cross-host adapter mechanisms reduce or reshape any future Harness residual gap before repository-owned implementation is considered.
cohortContract.accountAndDataBoundary: Public Git objects only; no private repository, account connection, credential use, telemetry call, or candidate runtime.
cohortContract.inactiveIsolation: Partial clones were created under one operating-system temporary root outside every Agent Skill, Plugin, App, MCP, Hook, manager, and consumer discovery root.
cohortContract.stopRule: Stop after all three pre-existing system-or-manager-only sources have a current default-branch revision, exact selected Git-object manifest, lifecycle and authority review, and one reference-only disposition. Do not expand into their Skill catalogs or search for additional systems in this cohort.

limitations: The observation binds the named default-branch revisions and selected Git objects on 2026-08-06; it does not prove future branch state.
Static source review does not prove runtime correctness, security, portability, behavior, value, or compatibility with current live manager state.
Selected-object manifests are review slices, not claims that every file in the three repositories was semantically reviewed.

mechanismFindings: The source combines an installer, Claude global hooks, multi-backend model execution, manual or automatic Skill injection, worktree creation, parallel execution, session resume, and log cleanup rather than supplying one bounded manager primitive.
The installer defaults to a user-level Claude root and supports run-command operations, overwrite, update, uninstall, status backup, and rollback.

The multi-backend wrapper defaults the Codex path to approval-and-sandbox bypass unless an environment flag disables it, and defaults the Claude path to permission skipping unless separately disabled.
Its worktree creation primitive is useful comparison input, but it creates branches and worktrees directly and does not bind the Harness authority, acceptance, handoff, or cleanup contracts.
sources.dispositionReason: The worktree, session, and rollback mechanisms are useful comparison inputs, but default permission bypass, live-root installation, Hooks, model execution, AGPL obligations, and whole-system scope make direct adoption or manager substitution ineligible.
sources.futureRecheckTrigger: A task-bound residual orchestration gap remains after current host thread/worktree support and safer reviewed alternatives, with separate model, permission, installation, and license authority.

mechanismFindings: The CLI provides broad source discovery, temporary prompt generation, per-agent path mapping, a canonical .agents/skills copy, symlink or copy projections, and a state lock containing source and folder-hash metadata.
The canonical-path and cross-agent mapping are useful adapter inputs for consumer-topology comparison, while skills.sh is a useful discovery surface already integrated by CC Switch.
Direct add, update, and remove operations write Agent roots; installation cleans the destination before copying, and a failed symlink falls back to an independent copy.

The reviewed source does not establish a CC Switch-compatible database, backup, default-enabled state, whole-cohort transaction, or rollback contract; its direct install route therefore does not preserve current manager authority.
sources.dispositionReason: Reuse skills.sh discovery and selected topology ideas through CC-owned lifecycle or a separately reviewed adapter; do not execute the direct installer into live roots or treat it as a replacement manager.
sources.futureRecheckTrigger: CC Switch exposes a verified import or atomic cohort interface, or an evidenced consumer-topology gap requires a separately reviewed adapter against this exact upstream behavior.

mechanismFindings: The source explicitly models an operator surface, host adapters, worktree and session runtime, observability and evaluation, promotion, and rollback, overlapping several Harness research questions.
It supplies selective install planning, dry-run, install-state, repair, uninstall, backup, adapter compliance, status, and bounded evaluator concepts that are useful comparative method inputs.

It is a large harness and distribution system spanning Agent roots, rules, Hooks, MCP templates, memory, plugins, Git hooks, global configuration, external packages, hosted GitHub integration, and account or credential boundaries.
Its own documentation marks host parity and some Codex plugin-loading behavior as limited; static repository presence and package counts cannot prove cross-host lifecycle behavior or value.
sources.dispositionReason: Compare specific mechanisms when a matching Harness gate opens, but do not bulk import, install, execute, or substitute the whole system for the current manager or portable decision core.
sources.futureRecheckTrigger: A bounded Harness mechanism gate has an exact comparator need for selective install planning, install-state recovery, adapter compliance, observability payloads, or promotion-and-rollback loops.
